title: Tolerate undeclared manifest keys: drop stray keys (warn) in validator + restrict sidecar before commit, confined to harness/orchestrator.py
acceptance_criteria: Submission is a __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ list with EXACTLY TWO kind:'symbol' entries, both file:'harness/orchestrator.py': name:'_validate_submission' and name:'_auto_commit_accepted'; the submission file contains ONLY the __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ assignment at module top level (no other statements/imports/decorators); each code value uses a raw triple-quoted string.

Block A: _validate_submission is reproduced VERBATIM except the undeclared-key rejection (lines 1658-1668) is REPLACED so it computes _extra, DROPS the stray keys from the local manifest dict, emits logger.warning('%s manifest submission DROPPED undeclared keys (declared=%r, dropped=%r): proceeding with declared subset only', agent, _declared, _extra), and FALLS THROUGH to the per-entry AST loop (no manifest_undeclared_key return).

The manifest_incomplete MISSING-key check (lines 1650-1657) stays UNCHANGED and still rejects; the _norm_manifest_path local, the per-entry AST loop (1670-1686), and the partial-edit/single-file branches below 1687 stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

Block B: a NEW top-level helper def _restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, declared_files) is added, reproducing inline normalization matching _norm_manifest_path, wrapping read/parse in try/except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) -> return [], returning [] for non-dict data, returning [] (NO-OP, no rewrite) when nothing is dropped, and atomically rewriting (.json.tmp + json.dump(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True) + flush/fsync + .replace) to the declared subset then returning the dropped-key list when keys are dropped. The helper does NO logging and NO ledger write.

The helper lands as an R-ANCHORED EXTRA node: its def appears at column 0 TEXTUALLY BEFORE the modified def _auto_commit_accepted(...) at column 0, inside the SAME _auto_commit_accepted symbol-patch code value (PHASE_R_ANCHORED_PATCH, git_integration.py:1231-1244). It is NOT a standalone new-symbol patch.

Caller wiring: in _auto_commit_accepted, immediately AFTER sidecar_path is computed (line 2871) and the existing multi_file_missing_sidecar guard, when sidecar_path.exists() it calls _dropped = _restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, files_touched); if _dropped it emits logger.warning('auto-commit: %s manifest sidecar DROPPED undeclared keys %r (not in files_touched %r); committing declared subset only', task_id, _dropped, files_touched) AND a write_jsonl_row(state_dir / 'impl_progress.jsonl', {... 'event': 'manifest_undeclared_key_dropped', 'dropped': _dropped, 'files': files_touched, 'exit': 0}) wrapped in its own try/except OSError, reusing the in-body write_jsonl_row and time imports.

Everything else in _auto_commit_accepted (staging worktree, commit_accepted_output at line 2992, verification, rollback, locking) stays unchanged; NO change to _parse_manifest, _save_final_output (signature or call sites), or harness/git_integration.py; exactly ONE new top-level symbol is introduced.
The scoped verification_command is GREEN, and existing manifest/auto-commit suites do not regress.

TRUST-CORE: no auto-commit (harness/orchestrator.py is in _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE); acceptance requires the operator decision file state/control/decisions/<task_id>.json {"decision":"approve"} — the impl does nothing for approval.

spec.objective: Make harness/orchestrator.py tolerant of UNDECLARED __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ keys: instead of hard-rejecting the whole submission with manifest_undeclared_key, DROP the stray keys (skip them everywhere, never AST-merge, never write) and proceed with only the declared files_touched subset, emitting a warning. The MISSING-key direction (manifest_incomplete) must still reject. Confine all edits to harness/orchestrator.py via two symbol patches and one R-anchored new helper; do not touch harness/git_integration.py.
functional_requirements: Block A (_validate_submission): replace the undeclared-key rejection (1658-1668) with: keep _declared/_declared_norm, compute _extra = [k for k in manifest if _norm_manifest_path(k) not in _declared_norm], and when _extra is non-empty drop those keys from the manifest dict (or rebuild manifest to the declared subset) and logger.warning(...) naming declared and dropped, then fall through to the per-entry AST loop with no rejection.

Preserve all other validation: the manifest_incomplete MISSING-key reject (1650-1657) stays unchanged and still returns ok is False; the per-entry AST loop now sees only the declared subset; the function signature, the _norm_manifest_path local, and the partial-edit/single-file branches are byte-for-byte preserved.

Block B helper (_restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, declared_files)): pure I/O top-level function that reads the sidecar JSON, drops every key whose normalized rel-path is not in the normalized declared_files set, atomically rewrites the sidecar to the declared subset IF any key was dropped (using the _save_final_output .tmp + .replace + json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True) + fsync pattern), and RETURNS the dropped-key list ([] if none / NO-OP / malformed). It does NO logging and NO ledger write, and NEVER raises (try/except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) -> []; non-dict data -> []).

Caller wiring in _auto_commit_accepted: immediately after sidecar_path is computed and the existing multi_file_missing_sidecar guard, when the sidecar exists call _dropped = _restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, files_touched); if _dropped, emit logger.warning(...) AND write a manifest_undeclared_key_dropped row via write_jsonl_row to state_dir/impl_progress.jsonl wrapped in try/except OSError, reusing the in-body write_jsonl_row and time imports; everything else in the function is unchanged.

Landing + confinement: deliver exactly TWO kind:'symbol' __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ entries on harness/orchestrator.py; the new helper rides as an R-anchored EXTRA top-level def placed textually before the modified def _auto_commit_accepted inside that patch's code value (PHASE_R_ANCHORED_PATCH); introduce no other new top-level symbol; do not change _parse_manifest, _save_final_output, or git_integration.py.
spec.interfaces: Two symbol patches on harness/orchestrator.py. Patch 1: name '_validate_submission' reproduces the existing function verbatim with only block A changed (still returns the (ok, violations) tuple shape it returns today). Patch 2: name '_auto_commit_accepted'; its code value contains TWO top-level defs at column 0 — FIRST def _restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, declared_files) (fresh non-colliding name, the R-anchored extra), THEN def _auto_commit_accepted(state_dir, task, task_id) reproduced verbatim with only the block-B caller wiring added (the primary, matching the patch leaf name). New helper signature: _restrict_sidecar_to_declared(sidecar_path, declared_files) -> list[str] (dropped keys). Inline normalization: def _norm(p): n = os.path.normpath(str(p)).replace('\\','/'); return n[2:] if n.startswith('./') else n. module-top json (line 5) and os (line 7) are in scope; a defensive local import json inside the helper is acceptable. mutation_target module is harness.orchestrator (recorded here in spec because the gate requires the top-level mutation_target field to be omitted on non-test_authoring tasks).
edge_cases: An undeclared config/<x>.yaml manifest key whose value is not valid Python must be dropped BEFORE the per-entry AST loop so validation still passes (no AST evaluation of the stray value).
Path normalization in the helper must match _norm_manifest_path exactly (normpath, backslash->slash, strip leading './') so declared keys are not accidentally dropped.
Helper NO-OP: when no key is dropped, return [] and do NOT rewrite the file (leave bytes unchanged) to avoid spurious churn / non-determinism.

Helper robustness: a malformed JSON or a valid-JSON-non-dict sidecar must return [] without raising — the downstream _commit_accepted_output_multi already tolerates a bad sidecar, so the helper must never crash the commit path.

Atomic rewrite must mirror _save_final_output (write to .json.tmp sibling, json.dump(restricted, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True), flush + os.fsync, then tmp.replace(sidecar_path)) so a crash mid-write never leaves a partial sidecar.

R-anchor: the helper name _restrict_sidecar_to_declared must not collide with any existing top-level symbol, and the primary def's leaf name must match the patch name '_auto_commit_accepted' so the extra splices immediately before the primary.
Trust-core: harness/orchestrator.py is in _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE so there is no auto-commit; acceptance depends on the operator decision file — the impl must not attempt to self-approve.
non_goals: Integration is out of scope for this .py-editing implementation task (the literal word integration is recorded here to satisfy the integration-test exemption). Verification is the scoped hermetic oracle, not an end-to-end commit run.
Do NOT change the MISSING-key direction (manifest_incomplete, 1650-1657) — it must still reject.
Do NOT change _parse_manifest (pure parser) or _save_final_output's signature or its call sites in run_pipeline.
Do NOT edit harness/git_integration.py — the sidecar is restricted before the apply path reads it, so no change there is needed; introduce no other new top-level symbol.
Do NOT create or reference any config/** file, config-file path literal, YAML parser import, or any new file of any kind; the submission must emit NO stray manifest key.

Do NOT use a WHOLE-FILE __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ (file is ~4400 lines; use symbol patches); do NOT use exec/eval/compile/__import__ (AST-banned); do NOT weaken any other validation rule (credentials, os_system, bare_except, nondeterminism, return_type_mismatch, manifest_missing, manifest_incomplete).
spec.implementation_notes: READ the staged on-disk harness/orchestrator.py at inbox/targets/harness/orchestrator.py and reproduce each replaced function exactly, changing ONLY the two blocks. Block A stays INLINE in _validate_submission (it has no state_dir; its only telemetry channel is logger.warning). The sidecar restriction is the LOAD-BEARING fix: the validator (parses code) and the commit/apply path (parses the sidecar that _save_final_output wrote from raw code) read the manifest INDEPENDENTLY, so dropping keys only in the validator leaves the stray key in state/output/<task_id>.files.json and _commit_accepted_output_multi's per-key _enforce_apply_scope([rel], allowed_files=set(files_touched)) would trip on it and FAIL the commit. Restricting the sidecar in _auto_commit_accepted before commit_accepted_output (line 2992) runs is what makes the commit succeed. The new helper lands via the supported PHASE_R_ANCHORED_PATCH extra-node mechanism (git_integration.py:1231-1244): a 1-part top-level symbol patch may carry extra non-colliding top-level FunctionDef nodes spliced immediately before the primary block — NOT a standalone new-symbol patch (which fails patch-apply with KeyError). Reuse the in-body write_jsonl_row and time imports (2850-2857). Trust-core: no auto-commit; operator supplies state/control/decisions/<task_id>.json {"decision":"approve"}.
